newsitem.title: USA: Air cargo industry soars into cyberspace.
newsitem.headline: Air cargo industry soars into cyberspace.

text.p: Arrow Air, the all cargo carrier, will soar into cyberspace on Monday with a site on the Internet, an official said Thursday.
Earlier this month Amerijet International Inc., a Fort Lauderdale-based cargo airline, also went on line.
"It is a marketing tool and communications tool," said Kevin Green, Arrow's director of sales and marketing. Arrow's page will show schedules, published rates, contact numbers and other information.

Amerijet's page provides information on routes, charter and trucking operations, equipment, facilities and company news. Visitors to Amerijet's site can request specific information on schedules and shipping requirements.
Although passenger airlines and integrators such as Federal Express Corp have extensive web pages, most U.S. cargo carriers are just beginning to establish sites.
Southern Air Transport of Columbus, Ohio, has been on the net since April and its pages have been viewed 1,487 times, said David Sweet, administrator of corporate communications.
"It is another arrow in the quiver," said Sweet.

Fine Airlines Inc of Miami, is considering entering the Internet. "Fine Air is constantly reviewing improved methods regarding the use of electronic communications with our customers and our interline partners. Entry onto the Internet is currently being reviewed," said its vice president Hugh Nash.
The International Air Cargo Association (TIACA) has a page and can put up a hyperlink for any cargo line to link its page to TIACA's, an official said.
